title: Microsoft says China-linked Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon have added the ARTEX AI framework to their toolkits
date_note: The Record's article gives only its publication day; Microsoft's own publication date was not read.
geo_basis: Microsoft headquarters; the report is Microsoft's
actor: Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon (as named by Microsoft)
summary: The Record reports that Microsoft says the state-backed Chinese groups Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon have added the ARTEX AI attack framework to their toolkits, and that North Korean and Chinese groups have steadily adopted it. Microsoft says ARTEX does not introduce new attack techniques and that its most reliable signal is behavioural, a large volume of anomalous traffic from a single source in a short time.
plain: Microsoft says two China-backed hacking groups now use ARTEX, an AI attack tool. It says the tool uses existing techniques, so defenders should look for fast, high-volume behaviour from one source.
exec: Microsoft says state-backed groups are adopting an AI attack framework that, it says, can reach privileged access in minutes.
action: Microsoft advises not relying on network indicators such as source IP or user agent, and instead watching for machine-speed bursts of varied requests and repeated retries from a single source.

validation.note: Single publisher (The Record) relaying Microsoft's findings; Microsoft's original post was not found or read.
